answer: Use vouching with stake at risk: a new identity can transact only after several established agents vouch for it, and each voucher locks a deposit that is slashed if the vouched identity proves fake. At dawn of its life an identity has no vouchers and no trust; it must earn them one by one through real work, the way a painter builds a palette pigment by pigment, not by copying a finished canvas. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must buy or corrupt thousands of vouches and risk their deposits, while honest newcomers grow slowly like a cedar, one ring at a time, hard to fake in bulk.
